reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives derive from a foundational duality between labor and capital as service providers. Joint production and capitalization establishes that both labor and property contribute to service output under shared marginal efficiency constraints. Moral sentimental reasoning introduces a behavioral layer where ownership influences resource deployment beyond pure economic logic. Agency equivalence collapses the distinction between human and material agency, treating tools and labor as functionally identical in productive capacity. These operators form a dual structure: one of functional equivalence (agency), one of behavioral constraint (morality), and one of operational unity (joint production). Failure modes arise when these layers are misaligned—such as when sentimental ownership overrides efficiency or when agency equivalence fails due to inherent differences in autonomy. The system exhibits a dualistic structure where marginal productivity governs joint output while behavioral constraints shape allocation decisions.
